```{=html}
<template id="tpl-l5r-dice">
<div style="display: flex; flex-direction: column; justify-content: center; text-align: center;">
    <span id="pyscript-loading" style="font-size: 20px; color: darkred">Loading...</span>
    <div style="display:flex; gap: 30px; justify-content: space-around; text-align: center;">
        <span id="empirical" style="font-size: 20px; font-weight: bold;"></span>
        <span id="calculated" style="font-size: 20px; font-weight: bold;"></span>
    </div>
    <div class="status-field-border" id="fig" style="font-size: 20px; color: darkred; overflow: scroll;">Generating figure...</div>
    <div style="display:grid; gap: 30px; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; text-align: left;">
        <span style="font-size: 30px;" id="first-roll"></span>

        <div id="roll-container" style="display:grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr 1fr;">

                <select name="dice-roll" id="dice-roll" style="font-size:20px">
                    <option value=1>Roll 1</option>
                    <option value=2>Roll 2</option>
                    <option value=3>Roll 3</option>
                    <option value=4>Roll 4</option>
                    <option value=5>Roll 5</option>
                    <option value=6>Roll 6</option>
                    <option value=7 selected>Roll 7</option>
                    <option value=8>Roll 8</option>
                    <option value=9>Roll 9</option>
                    <option value=10>Roll 10</option>
                </select>
            </div>
            <div style="display:flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center;">
                <label style="font-size: 20px;" for="dice-keep">Keep</label>
                <select name="dice-keep" id="dice-keep" style="font-size:20px;">
                    <option value=1>Keep 1</option>
                    <option value=2>Keep 2</option>
                    <option value=3>Keep 3</option>
                    <option value=4>Keep 4</option>

            </div>

        <div id="table-container" class="sunken-panel" style="display: flex;justify-content: center; width: 100%"></div>
        <span style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; font-size: 1.2rem;text-align: left; white-space: pre-wrap;">
Gage Rowden 2026

This tool simulates the rolling mechanics of the Legends of the 5 Rings role-playing game.

The user chooses a number of ten-sided dice to roll and a number less than or equal to that number of dice to keep. The tool calculates the probability of achieving a target number of successes, and visualizes the results.

Upon opening, the tool simulates 10,000 rolls for each possible roll/keep combination. The probability is shown as both a proportion of successes to losses (empirical) and as the area of the estimated density curve (calculated).

The tool was written in Python, and the core logic of the roller is implemented in the following "roll_dice()" function, which uses a recursive approach to determine the final roll.
                                            <code style="width: 100%;">def roll_dice(roll, keep):
    assert roll >= keep, "roll must be ≥ keep."
    rolls = [randint(1,10) for _ in range(roll)]
    keeps = sorted(rolls)[::-1][:keep]
    for i in keeps:
        if i != 10: break
        keeps += roll_dice(1, 1)
    return keeps</code>
The function first generates a list of length "roll" of random integers between 1 and 10. The rolls are sorted in descending order, and the first "keep" amount of numbers are chosen. If any "keeps" equal 10, the function is called again with roll=1 and keep=1. This goes on until no more 10's are rolled.
        </span>
    </div>
</div>
</template>
```
